intro: You are now inside the Ephesus Museum, a museum in İzmir province, opened in 1964. This is the museum of the Ephesus excavations. Here you will meet the two statues of Artemis, along with the frescoes and sculpture from the Terrace Houses.
history: The museum at Selçuk holds what came out of the Ephesus excavations but could not be shown on site. Frescoes and sculpture from the Terrace Houses, finds from the city's daily life and objects from the cult of Artemis each have their own hall. If you have just walked through Ephesus, this is where you see the inside of the city — the display was arranged for exactly that.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Great Artemis and the Beautiful Artemis, then the Terrace Houses hall, the Eros on a dolphin and the finds from the gladiator cemetery.
facts: Did you know? What the egg-shaped protrusions covering the Artemis statues represent is still argued over: breasts, bulls' testicles, dates and votive pouches have all been proposed. Take a look and decide for yourself. The frescoes and mosaics of the Terrace Houses are here too, among the fullest surviving evidence of what the inside of a wealthy Roman home looked like.
outro: This brings our tour of the Ephesus Museum to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Thank you for your company, and enjoy your visit.
